Here is my best transcription. I have preserved spelling/capitalization as much as possible. Bracketed text marks uncertain readings.

…therein It was witnessed that in consideration of all principal moneys and interest secured by a certain herein recited Indenture of Mortgage dated eighth October one thousand nine hundred and fourteen made between the said Michael O’Hare of the one part and the said Susan Judge of the other part the said Susan Judge as Mortgagee thereby assigned and conveyed unto the said Michael O’Hare his executors administrators and assigns all the lands and hereditaments comprised in the said therein recited Indenture of Mortgage and therein described as All that the premises comprised in an Indenture of assignment dated the Sixth day of April one thousand eight hundred and ninety three and made between James Alexander Campbell of the first part Michael Angelo Galway of the second part and Thomas O’Hare of the third part and therein described as all that and those that four tenement and premises late in the occupation of the late John [Robb] and of Eliza Sterling containing twelve acres two roods and twenty seven perches of the late Irish plantation measure or thereabouts be the same more or less situate lying and being in the townland of Ballymurphy Barony of Belfast and County of Antrim and bounded on the East and North by a farm in the occupation of John Healey and on the South by a farm of land in the occupation of Adam Frew and on the North West by a farm in the occupation of James Ross together with the full use of a road leading to the Falls Road which said premises and road are shewn by the map thereon endorsed excepting thereout all mines minerals and royalties whatsoever all which said premises are now situate in the County of the City or County Borough of Belfast To Hold the same unto the said Michael O’Hare for all the residue then unexpired of the term of Ninety nine years granted by an Indenture of Lease dated thirty April one thousand eight hundred and sixty eight made between John McCance of the one part and Peter Leslie of the other part absolutely discharged from all principal money and interest already and of all claims and demands under the said therein recited Indentures of Mortgage and Further Charge which said Deed and this memorial as to the due execution thereof by the said Susan Judge are witnessed by Edward Cortney Solicitor and F Gardner typist both of 59 Royal Avenue in the County of the City of Belfast aforesaid Susan Judge seal Signed and sealed by the said Susan Judge in presence of Edward Cortney Solr Belfast & Gardner 59 Royal Ave Belfast. The before named Edward Cortney maketh oath and saith that he is a subscribing witness to the Deed of which the foregoing writing is a memorial and also to said Memorial that he was present and saw said Deed and Memorial respectively duly executed by Susan Judge and that the name Edward Cortney subscribed as a witness to said Deed and Memorial respectively is this deponent’s proper name and handwriting. And [Cortney] Sworn at 59 Royal Avenue in the County of the City of Belfast this 23rd day of January 1918 and I know deponent Before me James Clarke Comr Commissioner authorised to administer Oaths for the Supreme Court of Judicature in Ireland in and for said County.

A true Copy

**No. 29**
**Molony to Gleeson**
Regd. 26 Jany 1918 @ 50 mins after 12 o’c

To the Registrar of Deeds in Ireland

A Memorial of an Indenture of Release made the tenth day of January one thousand nine hundred and eighteen Between Jeremiah Molony of Ballymacanare, Croon, in the County of Limerick, farmer, of the one part and Margaret Gleeson of Main Street, Croon, in the County of Limerick, Widow, of the other part Whereby after reciting as therein It was witnessed that for the consideration therein the said Jeremiah Molony as Mortgagee did thereby grant unto the said Margaret Gleeson her heirs and assigns All that and those the lands hereditaments and premises expressed to be granted by the therein recited Indenture of Mortgage of the thirteenth day of June one thousand nine hundred and eleven in dwelling house with Offices at the rear thereof situate in the Main Street of Croon and the strip of ground extending to the River Maigue being being part of the lands of Stanneryard with the gardens of Croon and Athenaclown situate in the Parish of Croon Barony of Coshma and County of Limerick To Hold the said premises unto and to the use of the said Margaret Gleeson her heirs and assigns in fee simple discharged from all principal money and interest secured by said Indenture and any covenants for payment of same therein contained and which Indenture of Release as to the execution thereof by the said Jeremiah Moloney is witnessed by J. F. Cronin Manager Munster and Leinster Bank Limited Croon and P. G. Potter Accountant Munster and Leinster Bank Limited Croon Jeremiah Moloney seal Signed and sealed by the said Jeremiah Moloney in presence of J. F. Cronin Manager Munster & Leinster Bank Ltd Croon, P. G. Potter Accountant Munster & Leinster Bank Ltd Croon. The before named J. F. Cronin maketh oath and saith that he is a subscribing witness to the Deed of which the foregoing writing is a memorial and also to said Memorial that he was present and saw said Deed and Memorial respectively duly executed by Jeremiah Moloney and that the name J. F. Cronin subscribed as a witness to said Deed Release and Memorial respectively is this deponent’s proper name and handwriting. J. F. Cronin Sworn at Croon in the County of Limerick this 11th day of January 1918 and I know deponent Before me William H. Lyons J.P. for Co. Limerick.

A true Copy
[signature]
[signature]

**No. 30**
**McCoy to McCoy Junr**
Regd. 26 Jany 1918 @ 53 mins after 12 o’c

To the Registrar of Deeds in Ireland

A Memorial of an Indenture dated 4th October 1917 Between Thomas McCoy of Rasegan in the County of Tyrone farmer of the one part and Thomas McCoy junior of same place his son of the other part whereby It was witnessed that said Thomas McCoy as beneficial owner thereby conveyed to said Thomas McCoy junr a farm of land in the townland of Ratergan in the Barony of East Omagh and County of Tyrone containing about 34a. 0r. 22p then in occupation of said Thomas McCoy as tenant from year to year under lease, Thomas McCoy reserving a yearly rent of £12-0-0 to hold same premises after the death of said Thomas McCoy to said Thomas McCoy junior for the estate and interest of said Thomas McCoy therein and said Thomas McCoy covenanted with said Thomas McCoy junior to pay the yearly rent and outgoings as they accrued due and not to permit or suffer said premises to be evicted for non payment of rent and said Indenture also witnessed as therein and it was thereby declared that it should be lawful for said Thomas McCoy at any time or times within 2 years from the date thereof by Deed or Deeds under his hand and seal to revoke memorialising Deed or any part thereof which said Indenture as to the execution thereof by said Thomas McCoy and Thomas McCoy junior is witnessed by King Houston of Omagh in the County of Tyrone Solicitor and James Browne of Killean in said County farmer and this memorial as to the execution thereof by said Thomas McCoy is witnessed by said King Houston and James Browne. Thomas McCoy seal Signed and sealed by said Thomas McCoy in presence of first truly read & explained to him by King Houston before he put his mark thereto, King Houston, James Browne. The before named King Houston maketh oath and saith that he is a subscribing witness to the Deed of which the foregoing writing is a memorial and also to said memorial that he was present and saw said Deed and memorial respectively duly executed by said Thomas McCoy and that the name King Houston subscribed as a witness to said Deed and memorial respectively is this deponent’s proper name and handwriting. King Houston Sworn at Omagh in the County of Tyrone this 24th day of January 1918 and I know deponent Before me a Justice of the Peace for said County. Chas W. Hamilton.

A true Copy
[signature]
[signature]

---

The clearest genealogy-relevant item here is **No. 29: Jeremiah Molony to Margaret Gleeson**, involving property in **Main Street, Croon/Croom**, with witnesses from the Munster & Leinster Bank at Croon. The surname is written **Molony** in the margin and body, not “Moloney,” though the same family could of course appear under both spellings in records.
